fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: Division of the cytoplasm into separate daughter cells.
model.Key feature: Two daughter nuclei become enclosed within separate cells.
model.Example: Two daughter nuclei become enclosed within separate cells.
model.Important distinction: Nuclear division and cytoplasmic division are related but not identical.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: An inward constriction of an animal cell during cytokinesis.
model.Key feature: A dividing animal cell pinches inward at its middle.
model.Example: A dividing animal cell pinches inward at its middle.
model.Important distinction: A rigid plant cell wall prevents this same pinching mechanism.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: A developing partition that contributes to the new wall between dividing plant cells.
model.Key feature: Vesicles fuse in the middle of a plant cell to establish a separating partition.
model.Example: Vesicles fuse in the middle of a plant cell to establish a separating partition.
model.Important distinction: Plant cytokinesis builds a partition rather than simply pinching a rigid wall inward.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: A control mechanism that helps determine whether a cell proceeds to a later stage.
model.Key feature: A cell with damaged DNA pauses instead of immediately entering division.
model.Example: A cell with damaged DNA pauses instead of immediately entering division.
model.Important distinction: Checkpoint failure can contribute to uncontrolled division; rapid normal growth is not automatically cancer.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: The first meiotic division, in which homologous chromosomes separate.
model.Key feature: Members of each replicated homologous pair move to opposite poles.
model.Example: Members of each replicated homologous pair move to opposite poles.
model.Important distinction: Sister chromatids normally remain together during this division.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: Pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I.
model.Key feature: Maternal and paternal homologues align closely along corresponding regions.
model.Example: Maternal and paternal homologues align closely along corresponding regions.
model.Important distinction: This pairing differs from individual chromosome alignment in mitosis.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: A paired set of two replicated homologous chromosomes containing four chromatids.
model.Key feature: Two replicated homologues align as a four-chromatid unit.
model.Example: Two replicated homologues align as a four-chromatid unit.
model.Important distinction: A tetrad contains two chromosomes, not four independently counted chromosomes.

fields: Key features or what it does

model.Meaning: A division that reduces chromosome sets from diploid to haploid, as in meiosis I.
model.Key feature: One homologue of each pair enters each daughter cell.
model.Example: One homologue of each pair enters each daughter cell.
model.Important distinction: Reduced sets can coexist with chromosomes still having two chromatids.
